items.original_mathematical_context: Set theory: indexed Cartesian product ∏_{i∈I}X_i, the collection of functions/tuples selecting one x_i∈X_i for every index i.
items.source_backed_preliminary_definition: Given a set I and sets X_i for i∈I, the indexed Cartesian product ∏_{i∈I}X_i is the set of all functions x with domain I such that x(i)∈X_i for every i∈I.

sources.section: General indexed Cartesian product and choice function interpretation
Nonemptiness of products and axiom of choice

items.mathematical_edge_case_and_context_compa: For empty I the product is the singleton containing the empty function. If a factor is empty and I is nonempty the product is empty. Nonemptiness of an arbitrary product of nonempty sets is equivalent to the axiom of choice in ZF; do not silently assume it.

items.original_mathematical_context: Homological algebra: ith homology H_i(C_•)=ker(d_i:C_i→C_{i−1})/im(d_{i+1}:C_{i+1}→C_i) of a chain complex of modules.
items.source_backed_preliminary_definition: Let (C_i,d_i) be a chain complex of R-modules with d_i∘d_{i+1}=0. The ith homology is H_i(C)=ker(d_i)/im(d_{i+1}), an R-module because the image is contained in the kernel.

sources.section: Section 12.13, paragraph preceding Definition 12.13.4

items.mathematical_edge_case_and_context_compa: Differential index is homological, decreasing degrees. The quotient requires d_i d_{i+1}=0. For cochain complexes cohomology uses different indexing, not the same statement.

items.original_query: generated sigma-algebra from open family tau
items.original_mathematical_context: Measure theory: σ-algebra σ(𝒜) generated by an arbitrary family 𝒜⊆P(X), the least σ-algebra on X containing 𝒜; Borel case specializes to 𝒜=τ.
items.source_backed_preliminary_definition: For a set X and a family A⊆P(X), σ(A) is the intersection of all σ-algebras on X containing A. For the topology τ of X, the Borel σ-algebra is σ(τ).

sources.section: Sigma-algebra generated by a family
Definition 3.2.4 generated σ-algebra

items.mathematical_edge_case_and_context_compa: σ(∅)={∅,X} (identified as a one-element family if X=∅). Arbitrary generating family is allowed; not only open sets.

items.original_mathematical_context: General topology: arbitrary indexed open cover (V_i) of X, with union X and no finite-subcover requirement.
items.source_backed_preliminary_definition: A family (V_i)_{i∈I} of open subsets of a topological space X is an open cover of X when ⋃_{i∈I}V_i=X.

sources.section: Definition of open cover
Definition of open cover

items.mathematical_edge_case_and_context_compa: No finite subcover is required for a cover. The empty family covers X exactly when X is empty. A cover of a subset A⊆X only needs A⊆⋃_i V_i.

items.original_query: locally section-generated sheaf of ideals I⊆O_X
items.original_mathematical_context: Algebraic geometry: subsheaf of ideals I of O_X locally generated by sections over neighborhoods of points.
items.source_backed_preliminary_definition: A locally section-generated ideal sheaf I⊆O_X on a scheme X is a subsheaf of ideals such that for every point x some open neighborhood U admits a family of sections s_j∈I(U) generating I|_U as an O_U-ideal sheaf.

sources.section: Lemma 26.10.1, paragraph on locally generated ideal sheaves

items.mathematical_edge_case_and_context_compa: Do not silently assume a *finite* local generating family. On schemes locally section-generated ideal sheaves are quasi-coherent, but quasi-coherence is a consequence/equivalence in this setting, not merely a synonym for local finite generation.

items.original_mathematical_context: Strict 2-category theory: invertible 2-cell α:f⇒g in the hom-category C(X,Y), admitting a vertical inverse β:g⇒f satisfying vertical identity composites.
items.source_backed_preliminary_definition: In a strict 2-category, a 2-morphism α:f⇒g between parallel 1-morphisms f,g:X→Y is vertically invertible if there exists β:g⇒f with β∘_vα=id_f and α∘_vβ=id_g in the hom-category C(X,Y).

items.source_backed_preliminary_definition: On a probability space (Ω,F,P), a filtration (F_t)_{t≥0} is a family of sub-σ-algebras F_t⊆F such that F_s⊆F_t whenever 0≤s≤t.

items.original_mathematical_context: Module theory: isomorphism class of an R-module M under invertible R-linear homomorphisms, the equivalence class of all R-modules isomorphic to M; this source restricts representatives to finitely generated R-modules.
items.source_backed_preliminary_definition: Fix a ring R. Two R-modules M and N represent the same isomorphism class if there is a bijective R-linear map M→N; [M] denotes the corresponding equivalence class in a specified universe or collection of modules.

sources.section: Abstract: isomorphism classes of modules in a small class and set of representatives

items.mathematical_edge_case_and_context_compa: Without a size/universe restriction the collection of all R-modules is generally a proper class, not a set. The source context concerns finitely generated R-modules; do not change that to all R-modules without a size framework. Isomorphism need not mean equality of underlying sets.

items.original_mathematical_context: Algebraic geometry: canonical structure sheaf O_Spec(R) of commutative rings on Spec(R), with O(D(f)) identified with R_f for distinguished opens and restrictions compatible with localization.
items.source_backed_preliminary_definition: For a commutative ring R, the affine structure sheaf O_{Spec R} is the sheaf of rings whose sections over every principal open D(f) are naturally R_f, with the restriction maps induced by localization; its stalk at p is R_p.

sources.section: Section 26.5, Definition 26.5.3 structure sheaf and basis localizations

items.mathematical_edge_case_and_context_compa: Stalk R_p and sections R_f are different objects, even when at p∈D(f). The sheaf must glue consistently; it is not just the presheaf on all open sets defined by a naive assignment.

items.original_mathematical_context: Commutative algebra: minimal prime of a commutative unital ring, a prime ideal minimal under set inclusion among all prime ideals, not simply a prime ideal of minimal positive height.
items.source_backed_preliminary_definition: A prime ideal p of a commutative ring R is a minimal prime if there is no prime ideal q with q⊊p.

sources.section: Section 10.17, Lemma 10.17.2 on existence of minimal primes
Section 10.26 irreducible components and minimal primes

items.mathematical_edge_case_and_context_compa: A zero ring has no prime ideals, hence no minimal primes. Minimality is inclusion-theoretic; do not confuse with arbitrary smallest *positive* height.

items.original_mathematical_context: Set theory: reflexivity property of a binary relation R⊆S×S, namely (x,x)∈R for every x∈S.
items.source_backed_preliminary_definition: A binary relation R⊆X×X is reflexive if (x,x)∈R for every x∈X.

sources.section: Definition of reflexive binary relation

items.mathematical_edge_case_and_context_compa: For X=∅ the empty relation is reflexive vacuously. Reflexivity does not imply transitivity or symmetry.

items.original_mathematical_context: Category theory: natural isomorphism between two covariant set-valued functors, a natural transformation with an inverse natural transformation; in particular its component bijections satisfy naturality in Y.
items.source_backed_preliminary_definition: For covariant functors F,G:C→Set, a natural isomorphism η:F⇒G is a natural transformation for which each η_X:F(X)→G(X) is bijective, equivalently η has an inverse natural transformation. In particular η_Y:F(Y)≅Hom_C(A,Y) must satisfy naturality in Y.

items.original_mathematical_context: Probability theory: indexed family (A_i)_{i∈I} of measurable events A_i∈𝔽 in a common probability space.
items.source_backed_preliminary_definition: An indexed family (A_i)_{i∈I} of measurable events in a probability space (Ω,F,P) is a function i↦A_i from I into F; no independence condition is implied.

items.original_mathematical_context: Graded module theory: internal direct-sum decomposition M=⊕_{j∈ℤ}M_j into degree-indexed additive subgroups, so each element has finite homogeneous-component support.
items.source_backed_preliminary_definition: An internal Z-graded additive-group decomposition M=⊕_{j∈Z}M_j means each m∈M has a unique expression m=Σ_{j∈F}m_j for some finite F⊆Z and elements m_j∈M_j. For an R-graded module the scalar multiplication must also respect degrees.

items.original_mathematical_context: Sheaf theory: stalk F_x of a sheaf F on a topological space X at x, the filtered colimit of sections F(U) over open neighborhoods U of x with restriction transition maps; for the structure sheaf O_X of a scheme the stalk is a local ring.
items.source_backed_preliminary_definition: For a sheaf F on X and x∈X, the stalk F_x is colim_{x∈U}F(U) over open neighborhoods U of x with restriction maps; a germ is an equivalence class of local sections. When F=O_X for a scheme X, this stalk is a local ring.

items.mathematical_edge_case_and_context_compa: A stalk is not the ring of sections on a chosen neighborhood. For general sheaves of sets the stalk need not be a ring; for O_X it is.

items.original_mathematical_context: Category theory: an isomorphism H:E→E' of categories equipped with projections p,p' to C, satisfying p'∘H=p and having an inverse over C.
items.source_backed_preliminary_definition: Let p:E→C and p′:E′→C be functors. An isomorphism of categories over C is a functor H:E→E′ with p′H=p and a strict inverse H^{−1}:E′→E also satisfying pH^{−1}=p′.

items.original_mathematical_context: Field extension algebra: K-linear multiplication map m_α:L→L given by x↦αx; same typed construction used for field norm.
items.source_backed_preliminary_definition: For a field extension L/K and α∈L, multiplication by α is the K-linear endomorphism m_α:L→L defined by m_α(x)=αx. For finite extensions its determinant is the norm N_{L/K}(α).

items.original_mathematical_context: Real analysis/topology: open interval I⊆ℝ, possibly unbounded, such that for each x∈I there exists δ>0 with (x−δ,x+δ)⊆I; each point is interior to the real domain.
items.source_backed_preliminary_definition: An open interval in the standard real line is a set (a,b)={x∈R:a<x<b} with endpoints a,b∈R∪{−∞,+∞} and a<b, where infinite endpoints are permitted, so (−∞,∞)=R.

sources.section: Open intervals and infinite endpoints

items.mathematical_edge_case_and_context_compa: The empty set is open and order-convex but some sources exclude it from the term 'open interval' unless degenerate intervals allowed; candidate context explicitly requires a<b, so empty interval not included. Their proposed 'each point has interior neighborhood' condition alone does NOT characterize intervals (disconnected open sets also satisfy it): order-convexity is essential.

items.original_query: field of rational functions in an arbitrary set of indeterminates over k
items.original_mathematical_context: Field theory: rational function field k(X_i : i∈I), defined as the field of fractions of the polynomial algebra in an arbitrary set I of algebraically independent indeterminates over field k; polynomial elements have finite support.
items.source_backed_preliminary_definition: Let k be a field and I a set of formal indeterminates. The rational function field k(X_i:i∈I) is the field of fractions of the integral domain k[X_i:i∈I], whose elements are ratios f/g with f,g finite-support polynomials and g≠0.

items.original_mathematical_context: Category theory: fibre category E_U of a functor p:E→C over U∈C; objects are x∈E with p(x)=U and morphisms are arrows α:x→y in E whose image under p is id_U.
items.source_backed_preliminary_definition: For p:E→C and U∈Ob(C), the fibre category E_U has objects e∈E with p(e)=U and morphisms e→e′ in E mapping under p to id_U, with identities and composition inherited from E.

items.mathematical_edge_case_and_context_compa: E_U exists for a functor over C without needing fibration/cartesian lift axioms. Those assumptions are required for related pullback functors, not for the fibre definition.
